title_en: Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Procedure for Chinese Citizens Applying for Recognition of Divorce Judgments of Foreign Courts
full_text_en:
SUPREME PEOPLE'S COURT

Provisions on the Procedure for Chinese Citizens Applying for Recognition of Divorce Judgments Rendered by Foreign Courts

(Adopted at the 503rd Meeting of the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court on July 5, 1991, and issued by the Supreme People's Court via Notice Fa (Min) Fa [1991] No. 21 on August 13, 1991)

Article 1 For a divorce judgment rendered by a foreign court with which China has not concluded a judicial assistance agreement, a Chinese party may apply to the people's court for recognition of that foreign court's divorce judgment in accordance with these Provisions.

For a divorce judgment rendered by a foreign court with which China has concluded a judicial assistance agreement, the application for recognition shall be made in accordance with the provisions of that agreement.

Article 2 These Provisions shall not apply to the recognition and enforcement of judgments on the division of matrimonial property, maintenance obligations, or child custody contained in a foreign court's divorce judgment.

Article 3 To apply to a people's court for recognition of a divorce judgment rendered by a foreign court, the applicant shall submit a written application and attach the original copy of the foreign court's divorce judgment and a certified accurate Chinese translation. Otherwise, the application shall not be accepted.

Article 4 The application shall specify the following:

(1) The applicant's name, gender, age, work unit, and domicile;

(2) The country of the court that rendered the judgment, the outcome of the judgment, and the date thereof;

(3) The circumstances of service of process and appearance in court;

(4) The grounds for the application and the request;

(5) Any other matters that need to be stated.

Article 5 The application shall be accepted by the intermediate people's court in the place of the applicant's domicile. If the applicant's domicile is inconsistent with his or her habitual residence, it shall be accepted by the intermediate people's court in the place of the habitual residence.

If the applicant is not within China, the application shall be accepted by the intermediate people's court in the place of the applicant's original domicile in China.

Article 6 Upon receiving the application and examining it, if the people's court finds that it meets the acceptance conditions under these Provisions, it shall docket the case within seven days; if it does not meet the conditions, it shall notify the applicant within seven days that the application is not accepted and state the reasons.

Article 7 The people's court shall review the application for recognition of a foreign court's divorce judgment by forming a collegial panel composed of three judges. The ruling made thereby shall not be subject to appeal.

Article 8 After accepting the application, if the foreign court's divorce judgment does not indicate that it has become legally effective or the effective date, the people's court shall order the applicant to submit a certificate issued by the court that rendered the judgment proving that the judgment has become legally effective.

Article 9 If the plaintiff in the foreign court's divorce judgment is the applicant, the people's court shall order the applicant to submit relevant documentary evidence demonstrating that the foreign court that rendered the judgment has lawfully summoned the defendant to appear in court.

Article 10 The documentary evidence required under Articles 8 and 9 shall be notarized by a notarial authority of that foreign country and legalized by the Chinese embassy or consulate in that country. The applicant shall also provide a certified accurate Chinese translation thereof.

Article 11 If the defendant in the foreign court's divorce judgment, who resides within China, is the applicant and has difficulty submitting the documentary evidence and the notarization and legalization required under Articles 8 and 10, the foreign court's divorce judgment may be presumed to be authentic and to have become legally effective if the applicant can submit the foreign court's notice of appearance or summons for appearance.

Article 12 Upon examination, if a foreign court's divorce judgment falls under any of the following circumstances, it shall not be recognized:

(1) The judgment has not yet become legally effective;

(2) The foreign court that rendered the judgment has no jurisdiction over the case;

(3) The judgment was rendered in the absence of the defendant without lawful service of process;

(4) The divorce case between the parties is currently being heard by a Chinese court or has already been adjudicated thereby, or a divorce judgment between the parties rendered by a court of a third country has already been recognized by a Chinese court;

(5) The judgment violates the fundamental principles of Chinese law or endangers China's national sovereignty, security, or social public interest.

Article 13 Recognition of a foreign court's divorce judgment shall be made by way of a ruling. If none of the circumstances under Article 12 exist, the ruling shall recognize its legal effect; if any of the circumstances under Article 12 exist, the ruling shall dismiss the applicant's application.

Article 14 The ruling shall be made in the name of the "Intermediate People's Court of ××, People's Republic of China," signed by the members of the collegial panel, and affixed with the seal of the people's court.

Article 15 Once served, the ruling shall immediately become legally effective.

Article 16 An applicant for recognition of a foreign court's divorce judgment shall pay a case acceptance fee of RMB one hundred yuan to the people's court.

Article 17 If an application for recognition of a foreign court's divorce judgment is filed through an agent, a power of attorney signed or sealed by the principal must be submitted to the people's court. If the power of attorney is issued by the principal outside China, it must be certified by the Chinese embassy or consulate in that country.

Article 18 After a people's court has accepted a divorce lawsuit, if the plaintiff changes the claim to an application for recognition of a foreign court's divorce judgment, or if the defendant separately files an application for recognition of a foreign court's divorce judgment, neither application shall be accepted.

Article 19 After a people's court has accepted an application for recognition of a foreign court's divorce judgment, if the other party files a divorce lawsuit with the people's court, the people's court shall not accept it.

Article 20 Even if the marriage between the parties has been adjudicated by a foreign court, if no application for recognition has been filed with the people's court, this shall not prevent either party from separately filing a divorce lawsuit with the people's court.

Article 21 After the applicant's application has been accepted by the people's court, the applicant may withdraw the application, and the people's court shall issue a ruling granting the withdrawal. After withdrawing the application, the applicant may not file another application for recognition but may separately file a divorce lawsuit with the people's court.

Article 22 After the applicant's application has been dismissed, the applicant may not file another application for recognition but may separately file a divorce lawsuit with the people's court.
